items.headline: Anthropic's Revenue Passes OpenAI's as Qwen Ships Fast
items.excerpt: Anthropic's quarterly revenue topped OpenAI's, and Alibaba shipped a new model while skipping its benchmark numbers.

items.headline: Big Walk Loses Players Over Ten Lines of Code
items.excerpt: House House disclosed a tiny slice of AI-assisted code in Big Walk, and Steam reviews turned negative within a day.

items.headline: Big Checks and Bigger Promises
items.excerpt: Anthropic set its IPO price and lined up $26 billion in backers, while OpenAI and world governments pledged new ways to switch AI off.

items.headline: Anthropic's Suppliers Become Its Biggest Buyers
items.excerpt: Anthropic priced its IPO at $70 to $78 a share, and its own chip and cloud suppliers put up $26 billion of the order.

items.headline: Circle Mints Billions to Stand Still
items.excerpt: Stablecoin payments jumped 45 percent this year while supply grew just 0.4 percent, because AI agents spend every dollar the instant they get it.

items.headline: Apple Risks Losing the Engineer Who Fixed Siri
items.excerpt: Mike Rockwell may leave the Siri team he rescued, leaving Apple's next AI chief unnamed.

items.headline: Anthropic Caps Claude Sheets at 100,000 Cells
items.excerpt: Claude Sheets builds a spreadsheet by chat, but its own maker still sends heavy financial work back to Excel.

items.headline: America Runs Four Times Europe's Data Centers
items.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield's newest count puts the U.S. far ahead of Europe and Asia, while Gulf states race to build an alternative close to home.

items.headline: Beijing Stalls Nvidia's Approved China Chip Deal
items.excerpt: Washington cleared H200 sales to Chinese buyers in February, but customs holds and gray-market resales show the chips are barely moving.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO Draws Far More Orders Than Shares
items.excerpt: Investors ordered several times more Anthropic stock than the company plans to sell, even after bankers trimmed its price target twice.

items.headline: Trump Defends Huang as FBI Watch Predates Scandal
items.excerpt: Trump said he believes Huang's story that he missed the spy warning, though the FBI flagged it to lawmakers nearly a year earlier.

items.headline: A Lawyer Builds His Own Private AI Server
items.excerpt: A South Carolina trial lawyer wired eight discontinued Nvidia chips into a machine that drafts legal work and keeps client files off the cloud.

items.headline: Anthropic's Own Chart Shows a Hidden, Stronger Model
items.excerpt: Anthropic's newest system card shows an internal model beating Mythos 5.2, the model it shipped the same day.

items.headline: Fireworks AI Loses Data to Hackers Twice
items.excerpt: Fireworks AI, valued at $17.5 billion, lost customer data to hackers for the second time in weeks.

items.headline: Buyers Balk, Builders Barrel On
items.excerpt: Banks try to resell $500 million of AI data-center loans at a discount, the same day Anthropic, Nvidia and Mavria keep the buildout moving.

items.headline: Dubbing Actors Win Consent Over Their AI Voice
items.excerpt: SAG-AFTRA's new animation contract makes a studio ask before dubbing a voice with AI, while Amazon and Netflix test how far AI dubbing can go.

items.headline: Nvidia's Scandal Now Carries a $7.5 Billion Price
items.excerpt: A new report ties Jensen Huang's affair to $7.5 billion in chip sales to China, and Nvidia's stock is already paying for it.

items.headline: Sarvam Hires a Closer, and Resells China's Models
items.excerpt: Sarvam AI named a 30-year enterprise sales veteran its president the same week its own marketplace kept reselling a Chinese model cheaper than its flagship.

items.headline: AI Browsing Moves Into Your Existing Browser
items.excerpt: OpenAI closed its Atlas browser and Microsoft dropped Copilot Mode, both folding AI into browsers people already use, while Perplexity's Comet bets the opposite.

items.headline: Meta and Oracle Move AI's Risk to Lenders
items.excerpt: Hyperscalers report stable balance sheets while funding AI's buildout with stretched depreciation schedules and debt structured to land on bondholders first.

items.headline: Microsoft Workers Call Its AI Pace Too Costly
items.excerpt: A design director's stock award shrank for moving too slowly on AI, the same week Microsoft's profit rose 32 percent.

items.headline: Trump Says He Threatened an AI Boss With Jail
items.excerpt: President Trump told 60 Minutes he warned an unnamed AI company leader to expect jail time.

items.headline: Claude Coders Say Opus 5.5 Changed Overnight
items.excerpt: A viral post said Anthropic changed Opus 5.5 overnight on November 3; the one tracker built to catch exactly that found a steady line.

items.headline: Smaller Bets, Bigger Doubts
items.excerpt: Meta's finance chief quits for a startup that had to ration its own customers, while Ken Griffin still calls the whole AI trade a bubble.

items.headline: Fake Citations Outrun the Volunteers Who Catch Them
items.excerpt: Columbia's audit found fabricated citations in 1 of 435 papers this year, and unpaid peer reviewers absorb the shortfall artificial intelligence creates.

items.headline: Taiwan Curbs Short Selling, Taiex Jumps 4.9%
items.excerpt: A short-sale cap and a NT$500 billion fund sent Taiwan's Taiex up 4.9 percent Monday, with TSMC alone supplying 41 percent of the gain.

items.headline: The Beatles Won a Grammy With AI Noise Cleanup
items.excerpt: The Recording Academy's human-authorship rule let the Beatles win with an AI-cleaned John Lennon vocal, and its next test arrives Nov. 16.

items.headline: ChatGPT Work Keeps Absorbing OpenAI's Other Apps
items.excerpt: Three months after OpenAI shut Atlas, ChatGPT Work has absorbed Canvas and Operator's tools and now shares Codex's usage limit.

items.headline: Anthropic Buys $3.4 Billion in Turbines, Preps IPO
items.excerpt: Anthropic bought $3.4 billion in gas turbines from Caterpillar, skipped a wait that stretches past 2030, and opens its IPO roadshow the same week.

items.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.excerpt: Anthropic's new models top its own rivals on benchmarks it wrote itself, and the launch echoes a safety fight from five months ago.

items.headline: Muse Ember Matches Haiku's Score at a Third the Price
items.excerpt: Meta says its new Muse Ember model matches Claude Haiku 5.5's top score, and Alexandr Wang calls it smarter than GPT-6 Luna for less money.

items.headline: Google AI Studio Builds Google Maps Apps From One Prompt
items.excerpt: Google calls it a one-prompt, cost-free map builder. It tried nearly the same pitch last year and retired it after 224 days.

items.headline: PSI's Quantum Proof Spreads Fast, Verdict Lags
items.excerpt: Two days after Physical Superintelligence announced a proof of an 18-year-old quantum puzzle, online attention has multiplied while the mathematicians behind it have stayed quiet.

items.headline: Hinton Predicts a Blackout, Skips the Meltdown
items.excerpt: Geoffrey Hinton expects AI to black out a power grid or bank system within 14 months, the Chornobyl-scale failure he says skips the reactor.

items.headline: AI Can Dream. What Now?
items.excerpt: Claude now rewrites its own memory between sessions, and that turns every idle hour into time a machine can learn.

items.headline: Claude Code Replaces a Restaurant's Five Apps
items.excerpt: A smash-burger owner outside the software trade spent a year building his restaurant's software with Claude Code, skipping five paid apps.

items.headline: Ballots, Bytes and Billion-Dollar Bets
items.excerpt: Voters reject data centers nationwide, DeepMind cracks a legacy cipher, and OpenAI's money keeps moving anyway.

items.headline: Ziwen Xu Races AI Agents to Beat GTA 6
items.excerpt: A solo founder deployed looping Claude agents to out-build Rockstar's game, then hit the wall only human judgment and licensing lawyers could clear.

items.headline: Companies Cut Service Jobs Before AI Shows Results
items.excerpt: Gartner finds four percent of customer-service leaders got the payoff they expected from AI, while employers already cut thousands of jobs on the bet.

items.headline: Eminem and Elvis Catalogs Sue Suno Same Day
items.excerpt: Eight Mile Style and Elvis Presley's rights holders both sued the AI company on Nov. 6, saying it trained on unlicensed songs.

items.headline: Perplexity Charges $200 for an Agent Anthropic Includes
items.excerpt: Perplexity's new Teammates agent costs $200 a month on Max alone, while Anthropic bundles a rival agent into a $20 plan.

items.headline: DOJ Joins xAI's Suit, and Colorado Rewrites Its AI Law
items.excerpt: xAI sued Colorado, the Justice Department joined its case, and the state signed a weaker AI law seventeen days after a judge paused enforcement.

items.headline: Meta Trains Muse Wonder on a Gigawatt Plant
items.excerpt: Meta's Prometheus data center trained Muse Wonder on dedicated gigawatt power, and Ohio is still deciding who pays for it.

items.headline: Claude Code's Quiet Setting Leaks Passwords for Months
items.excerpt: Apiiro, a security research firm, found passwords and keys in 1,122 public copies of a Claude Code settings file.

items.headline: Nvidia's Board Investigates Huang Over Spy Allegations
items.excerpt: Jensen Huang admitted an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and Nvidia's board opened a formal investigation.

items.headline: Zuckerberg's Muse Now Builds Your Own Mini Apps
items.excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg previews Muse's Spaces tool, which tracks your other apps in the background, as critics warn Meta's agent already reaches too far.

items.headline: US Officials Tie Jensen Huang to Alleged Chinese Spy
items.excerpt: A new account says the Nvidia chief's tie to an accused Chinese spy was romantic, as the executive linked to him reportedly vanished months ago.

items.headline: Trillions, Task Forces and Trimmed Targets
items.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic both land under their funding targets, the Justice Department opens an AI task force, and auditors flag redacted evidence at Anthropic.

items.headline: Anthropic Pays the AP, Battles the Rest
items.excerpt: Anthropic paid the AP for election data as its fight with four Canadian publishers over free use drags on.

items.headline: Information and Finance Jobs Shrink as AI Blame Fades
items.excerpt: October's jobs report found growth in professional services and computer work, but the sectors AI reaches deepest, information and finance, kept losing jobs.

items.headline: PitchBook Values Databricks at $68.7 Billion
items.excerpt: PitchBook's own model prices the business at $68.7 billion, about a third of the $190 billion its investors just paid.

items.headline: Google Cuts AI Video Price, Skips Some Instructions
items.excerpt: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash drops to 7 cents a second and stretches clips to 15 seconds, but one review still routes real work elsewhere.

items.headline: Claude Learns to Dream and Fix Its Own Memory
items.excerpt: Anthropic's new dreaming step lifted one memory score from 13 to 48 percent, while a law professor's deleted files show judgment lags behind recall.

items.headline: Qwen Keeps Reaching for Alibaba's Own Cloud
items.excerpt: Twelve days after Cohere's report, outside labs have skipped testing it, Alibaba stays silent, and one replay found something messier than a backdoor.

items.headline: Hidden Anthropic Model Cracks an 18-Year Quantum Puzzle
items.excerpt: A secretive Anthropic model helped a tiny lab prove a quantum computing conjecture open since 2008, and only the proof itself is public.

items.headline: Investors Tell Anthropic Its IPO Price Is Too High
items.excerpt: Major investors want Anthropic's $1.5 trillion IPO value cut toward $1 trillion after Thursday's stock selloff.

items.headline: Spies, Slides and Shopping Bots That Still Buy Wrong
items.excerpt: Congress presses Nvidia over a Chinese tie, chip stocks lose $440 billion in a day, and Visa's AI shoppers still buy the wrong thing.

items.headline: Claude Code's Email Leak Exposes Anthropic's Bug Backlog
items.excerpt: A privacy bug sent user emails to websites for months while 98.2 percent of Anthropic's bug reports sat unassigned.

items.headline: Nvidia Calls an Alleged Spy a Customer
items.excerpt: Three House chairmen want Jensen Huang to explain his ties to Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive Nvidia calls an ordinary customer.

items.headline: Gold Explorers Point AI at the Safest Ground
items.excerpt: Gold exploration money increasingly aims AI at ground miners already hold, while hunts for brand-new deposits hit a record low.

items.headline: Disney's OpenAI Deal Collapses Before One Check Clears
items.excerpt: Disney promised OpenAI $1 billion for Sora access to its characters, and OpenAI killed the app three months later with $0 of it paid.

items.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic Expand H-1B Hiring as Rivals Retreat
items.excerpt: AI labs more than tripled H-1B filings under Trump's $100,000 fee while Amazon, Google and Microsoft pulled back, and two courts just blocked the charge.

items.headline: OpenAI Locks Its Strongest Hacking Model Away
items.excerpt: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber doubles its own model's price, demands a security review, and still misses more than half its benchmark's attacks.

items.headline: Microsoft Ends Its Oracle AI Cloud Deal
items.excerpt: Microsoft dropped a 2023 deal for Oracle's aging AI chips, and Oracle says buyers still want them at a premium.

items.headline: Cat Wu Quits Claude Code for OpenAI
items.excerpt: Cat Wu left Anthropic's Claude Code team and joined OpenAI days later, one of three Claude Code departures since Oct. 24.

items.headline: Moonshot Gives Away Its Biggest Model
items.excerpt: Moonshot released the full weights behind its 2.8 trillion parameter Kimi K3.1 Pro, free to run and sell, with one catch.

items.headline: Schools, Spending and a Skeptic's Spreadsheet
items.excerpt: Google ties school search to its AI, Michael Burry calls Anthropic's growth math pure optimism, and voters punish AI's biggest campaign spenders.

items.headline: Pentagon's AI Billions Bypass Its Smallest Suppliers
items.excerpt: The Pentagon's record AI budget flows to contractors already wired for audits, while a suspended rule leaves small suppliers outside the same systems.

items.headline: Judge Lee Keeps Anthropic's $3 Billion Case Alive
items.excerpt: Judge Eumi Lee dropped Dario Amodei's personal copyright claim but left Anthropic's bigger fight over Claude's lyrics unresolved.

items.headline: Oracle's OpenAI Bet Drags Its Credit Toward Junk
items.excerpt: S&P cut Oracle one notch above junk after OpenAI's deal grew to half its backlog, and bondholders say Oracle hid the math.

items.headline: Aina Charges $399 for What Rabbit Just Dropped
items.excerpt: Aina's new ring costs $399 to $499, the same hardware bet that sank Humane's Pin and that Rabbit dropped this September.

items.headline: AI Super PACs Back Seven Losers
items.excerpt: Leading the Future and Public First funded twelve competitive Nov. 3 races, and the side AI money backed lost in seven of them.

items.headline: Ansari's AI Ban Post Sinks Storage Stocks
items.excerpt: Rep. Yassamin Ansari's call to ban superintelligence helped drive Western Digital's stock down 13.5 percent, and three rival storage makers fell with it.

items.headline: Claude Starts Reading Bank Accounts, Stays Read-Only
items.excerpt: Anthropic's new Claude feature reads a bank balance and two years of spending, but security researchers say read-only access still leaves a risk standing.

items.headline: Twelve Machines Called the Senate. Inside BULX the Morning After.
items.excerpt: BULX's twelve agents backed Democrats at 64% before they won the Senate, and Nathan Scherner says what that proved.

items.headline: Claude Maps First 3D Vault Particle From Bacteria
items.excerpt: Anthropic used Claude to map a hidden cell structure, and a congresswoman demanded an AI pause the same afternoon.

items.headline: The Signal 2026-W45: Anthropic's IPO Doubts Mount As OpenAI Cuts Its Valuation
items.excerpt: Investor doubts over Anthropic's IPO timing and OpenAI's lower funding valuation signal a cooling AI market, as executives keep leaving Anthropic for OpenAI and Meta.
